nididhyāsana
(‘meditation’)
------------------------------------------
This is the term specially used in Vedānta to signify meditation. It has been defined as the stream of ideas of the same kind as ब्रह्मन् to the exclusion of all other ideas like those of the body. Ultimately it leads to समाधि or total absorption in ब्रह्मन्.

Nidrā
(‘Goddess of sleep’, ‘sleep’)
------------------------------------------
The Prādhānikarahasya (10), a supplementary text of the Devīmāhātmya describes निद्रा as a goddess and an aspect of Mahākālī. Iconographical works show her as a lady reclining on a couch.
Some texts like the Lakṣmītantra state that निद्रा is one of the four consorts of विष्णु, the other three being लक्ष्मी, Prīti and विद्या.
Other texts picture her as the wife of कालाग्निरुद्र, an aspect of रुद्र or शिव.
The word ‘nidrā’ is most commonly interpreted as ‘sleep’. This निद्रा has two aspects: स्वप्न (with द्रेअम्स्) and सुषुप्ति (dreamless sleep or deepsleep).
Patañjali (200 B. C.) defines निद्रा (vide Yogasūtras 1.10) as the वृत्ति or the modification of मिन्द् dependent on तमस् (darkness or इग्नोरन्चे), which is responsible for the absence of the waking (jāgrat) and the dream (svapna) states. It is actually deep (dreamless) sleep that is indicated here.
Nidrā is needed for the health of the body. When the three dhatus (basic हुमोउर्स् of the body) are in a state of equilibrium, good health is attained; and, sound sleep at the right time is an aid to this.
Whereas good sleep is denied to those who are stricken with poverty or disease or to the immoral persons, it comes easily to healthy persons as also who are pure in heart.
Yogic works describe that sleep overtakes a person when his मिन्द् enters the medhyānāḍī, one of the several nāḍīs in the human body.
The Māṇḍūkyakārikā (3.44, 45) consi-ders sleep—called ‘laya’ here—as one of the four obstacles to समाधि.
The Suśrutasaṁhitā (Śārīrasthāna 4.32) says that the hṛdayapuṇḍarīka (heart-lotus) closes and hangs upside down during sleep.
A funny story in one of the पुराणस् reveals that राम gave the boon to निद्रा, the goddess of sleep (after she left कुम्भकर्ण who was killed by राम) to reside in the hearts of those evil persons who try to listen to Rāmānāma or the पुराणस्, and in lazy students not interested in the acquisition of knowledge!
